description: An end-to-end LLM pipeline designs the game-state encoding for a probability-only model, decodes its outputs into game controls, and clears Sushi Survivors' beginner boss stage in 10 minutes of real-time play.
A Chrome extension uses Jev to classify YouTube Shorts on the fly and auto-skip ads and off-topic clips—surfacing only RESCENE videos—with fast, low-cost inference that tolerates occasional misses.

A six-agent pipeline grades memecoin launches before pools open using schema-guaranteed typed outputs (not strings) with calibrated probabilities, making 70ms decisions across 100K launches/1.4M judgments at $0.042/M input tokens—flagging rugs, bundles, and snipes like a drain it refused 26 minutes early.

An AI VTuber that reads chat comments and responds with speech, expressions, gaze, and gestures — Gemini generates replies, JEV controls Live2D motion/props, Aivis Cloud synthesizes voice — demoed in real time with all 196 Live2D parameters visualized.
A faithful recreation of the 1986 arcade game Gapper is played fully autonomously in realtime by an AI agent on autopilot.
An AI agent autonomously solves Minesweeper in real-time gameplay, perceiving the board state and reasoning through cell-by-cell mine deductions without human input.
Real-time timeline filtering that cleans up your X feed by automatically removing unwanted content as you scroll.

A text-driven 3D pocket garden pipeline chaining GPT-6 Astra (scene + interaction), Tripo (generated cottage/bench assets), and Jev (deciding what to move or keep) — with ambience swaps, movable trees/mushrooms, pause, and undo.
A playful AI-engineering demo of a Hunter x Hunter character/personality quiz app, built and tested as a fun side experiment.
A web game where you write ambiguous sentences that fit both sides of a binary choice (e.g., "dog vs cat", "sea vs mountain") to push the AI judge's confidence as close to 50/50 as possible.

Scraped 2,000 Meta beauty ads via Apify, read creatives with free-tier Gemini, and graded 302 ads on 9 dimensions with classifier Jev — 2,718 judgments in an afternoon for $0.0167, showing UGC ads (1.63/5) beat catalog ads (0.48) 3x.
A semantic search layer over the ACKS2 RPG's Monstrous Manual lets users instantly find any monster by description, with expansion to the full ruleset planned next.

author.name: Daniel Humphries - coffee x creative tech

description: An AI agent effortlessly triages and categorizes years of hoarded Twitter bookmarks in minutes, turning a cluttered archive into an organized, searchable library.
A voice assistant that listens to couples' arguments in real time, scores the partner's anger on a 1–10 scale, and generates de-escalation advice in 374ms.

Jev-1.13 classified 3,373 à-la-carte dishes into food types in 9.7s for $0.11 (2.56M input tokens), hitting 84.5% agreement with strictly typed labels—misses came from polysemous dish names, never hallucinated categories.
Swapping a 12-bot trading desk's narrative scorer for a 4-question typed-prompt call cut scoring latency from 2.3s to 190ms, capturing a 1 ETH memecoin entry the old pipeline would have missed.

JevFill is an MIT-licensed unpacked Chrome extension that uses TypeSafe's Jev to map freeform plaintext notes onto web form fields, highlighting filled fields green for review while never sending or filling password/payment inputs.

A "bouncer" pre-filter that sits in front of trading agents — checking each signal for LLM-worthiness, prompt injection, and clarity before it gets through — blocked 23 bad trades and one injection attempt in a single night, boosting returns from +1.9 to +4.2 ETH.
An OSS library and x402 API turn Vercel AI Gateway's free Jev into a text extractor by having the typesafe model return indexes into the input and slicing the text — no LLM needed.
Demo shows an AI dialogue tension evaluator scoring the same *A Few Good Men* line 75/100 in isolation but 95/100 once the preceding dialogue was added as context.

Jev filters your X timeline to one-click remove ads, abuse, and crypto shilling, adding flow-rate and time-based filters that outpace delayed third-party hot-post monitors for faster AI trend tracking.
A malicious link scanner for dub.co's link shortener was built in 2 hours using Jev, trained on 10K+ previously caught malicious domains to detect and flag abusive URLs at near-negligible token cost.

A token-less classifier is turned into a storyteller by looping it with a 1948-Shannon trigram proposer — 90 picks at 0.4 s and $0.00003 per word — revealing that generation splits into proposing vs. judging, and the proposer is the bottleneck.
A Pac-Man demo where an LLM agent controls the ghosts against a human player in real time, running a full game for under $0.01 at ~500ms average latency.
An AI agent is demoed playing unreleased 90s Japanese arcade games in real time, parsing live gameplay and generating control inputs on the fly.

A cellular-automaton-style sim where the Jev AI engine decides each cell's behavior from its characteristics—fully emergent with no scripted rules, already playable but still needing tuning for richer dynamics.

A typhoon dashboard pipes Japan Meteorological Agency disaster bulletins into type-safe Jev for relevance classification, answering 50 questions per bulletin in ~400ms including Tokyo-to-US-West-Coast round-trip latency.
Demo uses TypeSafe AI's Jev model to select avatars' facial/body expressions in real time during a scripted two-avatar conversation.
A WhatsApp scam-detection demo that triages 10,208 messages in 32 seconds for $0.065, flagging which ones would defraud the user's mother.
Astra-built controller hands live control of real Crossy Road to Jev, whose gameplay decisions stream visibly in real time.
Jev demonstrated lightweight, rapid AI categorization with a smooth workflow and broad potential for practical classification tasks.

SAM 3 + depth cameras feed 3D observations to parallel Jev calls that rank sampled grasp/placement poses, while deterministic IK controllers drive a simulated mobile robot through a nearly complete lid pick-and-place sequence.

A NERVE memecoin analyzer node pairs JEV's 190ms pool scoring with a four-layer pipeline emitting 14 typed, threshold-checked decisions per token at $0.001 each — flagging a rug at 0.93 confidence and dodging pools worth 4 ETH.
A cloud-based AI agent autoplays a typhoon-escape game better than its human operator, though open questions remain about whether cloud latency can sustain millisecond-critical real-time gameplay.
A mood-tracker demo built on Jev scores each typed sentence against six emotions in real time, coloring sections of a generated flower based on the strongest detected feeling.
Jev is demoed running semantic search over Mark Rothko's paintings, retrieving matching artworks from just a few descriptive words.

A Jev-powered X copilot that scores every post in your feed on niche relevance and audience value, then recommends whether to reply, quote, like, bookmark, or skip — turning scrolling into structured, intentional engagement.
An agent built on TypeSafe's Jev decision-making model scans the Downloads folder, classifies each file, and automatically deletes the unneeded ones.
A Godot demo runs an autonomous NPC war with two teams of independently decision-making units, with combat quality improving further after switching to a different model.

A landing page audit tool that takes a URL, extracts headings, copy, and CTAs, answers 30 typed evaluation questions in one pass with probability-backed scores — costing $0.00024 and ~1.1s per page (Stripe scored 81).

An agent gates every proposed action through Jev, a millisecond conscience that scores reversibility, budget, data support, downside, prior rejections, and confidence for ~$0.001 per decision—holding on any red flag and alerting the user.

A single-prompt agent harness demo where Astra plans and reviews while a Gemini swarm builds a working Minecraft factory sorter, with TypeSafe's new Jev language deciding item routing in real-time gameplay.
Jev, a fast structured-output model, classifies text demands as HARD or SOFT constraints for routing tasks, returning answers in under a second.
A locally-tuned AI agent plays Advance Wars-style turn-based strategy matches autonomously—fielding a smaller Orange army with no turn limit, winning by wiping out the enemy or capturing their HQ.
A real-time AI agent ingests live game state and selects winning next moves in Street Fighter with impressive speed.

An agent drives a browser by compressing each DOM into an element table, letting an LLM pick the action and element per step via a single OpenRouter call—no screenshots, ~200 bytes and ~$0.0001 per step.
A semantic log filter built on Jev, exposed through a CLI so AI agents can query logs programmatically and wrapped in a custom TUI for interactive searching.
A movie recommendation engine built with jev, experimenting with ranking personalized film suggestions.

A real-time Plato avatar mockup that uses jev to drive facial expressions and avatar state directly from live conversation, demoed answering "what's the meaning of life?" for game NPCs, teaching avatars, and companion apps.

Jev does live deal qualification during sales calls, re-scoring every qualification question with confidence every 2 seconds in a single request—costing ~$0.17 per 30-min call (80% cheaper)—so empty fields surface as the seller's next question while the buyer is still on the line.

A racing game where an AI driver built with Claude Code picks racing lines and braking points from speed and corner data, and—having no memory—re-optimizes each lap by reviewing all 11 corner split times to decide where to push harder.

Giving an LLM maze-solving judgment only at junctions while code holds the DFS stack and visited set solved a 14×14 braided maze in 22 calls and 56 steps (2.2× optimal), versus 60 per-step calls that just paced a 7-cell corridor at 96% confidence.

A safety guardrails demo showing real-time risk warnings that appear mid-typing and adapt instantly as `rm -rf ./build` becomes `rm -rf /`, validated on a 200-command labeled dataset with results benchmarked in the video.

A custom Chrome extension built with TypeSafe AI "Jev" auto-fills a 15-field form in just 1.2 seconds by skipping text generation and returning only structured data — a perfect match for browser automation.

description: JEV analyzes millions of Reddit comments and posts in seconds, using k-means clustering to automatically discover and group content into topics for large-scale categorization.
AI agent jev paired with HyperFrames delivers near-instant video editing—automatically cutting bad takes, guiding effects, and handling style work with minimal manual effort.

A media-art prototype that classifies your own Slack posts and piles them up like an hourglass, letting you compare post types across multiple categorization axes—built in a day, showing how modern tooling lets creators focus on expression immediately.
A reusable LLM ranking loop scores tweet drafts against 88 criteria distilled from prior viral posts in 0.92s for $0.00016 per check, then flags the next edits until the score plateaus.
A Jev-powered game converts prompt words into Kyoto dialect in real time, showing small LLMs can handle lightweight natural-language tasks despite untuned prompts.

An "AI-smell" checker that numerically scores how AI-generated text sounds using real Jev measurements, built with Codex and rendered into an MP4 demo via HyperFrames and FFmpeg on TypeScript/Node.js.
A fully local Chrome extension that uses the Jev model to filter your X feed in real time, hiding everything except genuine, relevant posts worth replying to.
An AI categorization demo uses Jev to score 2,952 museum objects on whether each one qualifies as architecture.
Demo uses JEV attention scores to route a user's voice conversation to the agent most likely to answer, while in parallel ranking mood scores to update each avatar's props in real time.

A typed AI agent outputs structured visual mood parameters—color, brightness, and motion—reduced to mood probabilities, intensity, and an unresolved value, driving seamless hot-reloaded WGSL shader changes through a Vite + Metal pipeline.

Game NPCs run as autonomous AI agents with persistent memories and DNA-shaped personalities: Jev selects a character's response intent from their profile in 0.48s, then GPT-5.6 Luna renders it as dialogue.
A Swift emoji picker app that predicts and surfaces the top three relevant emojis in real time as the user types.

A custom open-source TUI benchmark for turn-based strategy runs renders full game state (map, hand, energy, enemy intents, status effects, relics, blocks) alongside live agent telemetry (choices, confidence, action probabilities, latency) for transparent, non-black-box evaluation.

Pairing an agentic search tool with an LLM to sift securities reports, press releases, and disclosures across listed companies—broad-scanning 145 firms then narrowing to 34 matches, with precision still a work in progress.
A Karpo experiment uses Jev to learn taste from Google Maps history and probabilistically rank 1,253 NYC places, faster and cheaper than querying an LLM for each location.

A browser-based Three.js anime skateboarding game (AFTERLIGHT) with 20 dynamic sky/lighting looks and an LLM-powered "Ride Director" that translates natural-language prompts like "fast and close" into ride modes and camera settings.
A demo repurposes the Jev LLM into a country ranker that scores and orders nations against a chosen criterion.

An app turns spoken monologues into generative art: Gemini transcribes audio, a 12-color emotion-cue logic picks hues, Claude writes the JavaScript that paints the canvas, and a Tone.js MIDI layer turns it into melody — words become painting become song.
An autonomous browser agent scraped 4 rental sites in 1m16s for $0.0454, visiting 32 pages across 76 actions and 112 model calls to return 21 houses.

An open-source Chrome extension that detects Taobao/JD.com listings from merchants suspected of denying staff two-day weekends and stamps a "PASS" overlay on them as you scroll, letting shoppers vote with their wallets.

Benchmarked an LLM judging 4,005 underground Chinese deal wires where sellers evade platform detection via deliberate homophone misspellings (券→卷, 元→亓): p50 724ms, fastest 515ms, $0.0206 total, 63% routed to nobody.
Set up the trending Jev agent to automatically categorize the news articles delivered in their personal morning briefing each day.

description: A demo auto-classifies 300 Notion meeting-note items into 5 customer issue categories at noticeably high speed, showcasing how to offload routine classification and pass/fail judgments from Claude.

Open-source terminal agent "Jev" trades Polymarket's 5-minute BTC Up/Down markets: each tick it reads market + spot state, emits a side with calibrated confidence, and a deterministic policy enters only above a hard confidence/edge gate once per window.
A waste-sorting demo classifies item names under Osaka-style rules, returns confidence-scored categories like “plastic resources 88%,” and defers low-confidence calls to a human.

description: A WebGPU-native demo where Jev autonomously assesses a space station scenario, weighs evacuation risk and urgency, and directs drone rescue actions at 208 ms average response including network latency, rescuing all 12 crew.

Built with Jev, this app live-transcribes Japanese business meetings — every 4s speech becomes text, key points stream, issue cards pile up, and "next move" suggestions update — framing Jev as an option-generating AI.

description: An amenity icon picker built on Phosphor icons that maps landlords' unstructured listing amenities to standardized visual icons for categorization.

"Seat Oracle" hackathon app scores pairwise compatibility between attendees from their X profile text, then uses simulated annealing to auto-generate event seating—turning AI matchmaking into a game while cutting organizer workload.

A probabilistic decision model plays a 60 FPS 80s-style arcade shooter, choosing ship position, firing, and attack/dodge/wait actions from compact game states while the engine handles collisions, projectiles, and escalating mob waves.
Sorting 20,000 emails into 4 bins in 4.6 seconds for $0.15—versus Claude Haiku's 70 seconds and $1.74—trades 0.2% accuracy (99.7% vs 99.9%) for a 15x speedup and 12x cost cut.
An infinite backrooms game where the environment is AI-generated in real time as you explore—no premade map—with each room costing ~$0.000265 to generate.

A fully autonomous cloud trading bot that scans open markets every 5 minutes, sizes positions by how far real signal has pulled ahead of posted odds, pays its own hosting bill, and compounded $50 into $8,310 in 22 hours after dropping to $7 at hour two.

An AI agent plugged into a driving game navigates city traffic autonomously — stopping for pedestrians and crossing cars, slowing for corners and potholes — making stop/yield/slow/proceed decisions while local code handles steering and collision checks, with a live status HUD, all for $0.0208 per city drive.
Jev, an AI layer making final outfit decisions in aesty, detected deliberately hidden toe shoes in a party look and restyled the rest using the user's existing wardrobe in 3 seconds for $0.0015.

An AI agent's terse outputs were re-engineered into full-sentence responses via prompt or output-layer modification, demonstrating lightweight control over an LLM's response format without retraining.

An LLM agent re-read notes on 8,690 cold CRM deals in 7m41s for $0.43 (~145 human-hours of work), flagging 4,422 dead leads, 300 lapsed call-backs, 263 unfulfilled promises, and ranking 633 deals worth re-calling.

A dual-model bot clones 100+ top memecoin wallets on Robinhood Chain—rescanning every 20s, filtering wash trades, scoring 536 wallets—then fires ≥80%-confidence $100 trades with hard stop-losses: 52,110 decisions in 21.6s for $0.37 API cost.
A simulated miniature city runs in real time using Jev, showcasing virtual agent behaviors in a small-town environment.
An AI pipeline evaluated 60 TikTok UGC videos across 3 product niches for viral potential in 1.9 seconds for $0.0022 total.

A low-cost, high-speed model ("Jev") powers a POC that scores command opsec in real time inside Mythic C2 and classifies expression types—promising for offensive security despite still-limited cyber skill.

Jev indexes the Katagami art-style library for humans and agents (via MCP), parsing each ask into traits and ranking style candidates for fit in ~1s — impossible with embeddings alone — and replacing deterministic publishing checks.

Tiny World is an interactive 3D simulation of six autonomous residents with homes, jobs, needs, and friendships whose next actions are decided by an LLM, letting you inject scenarios like emergencies and watch their society react.
A real-time AI agent plays Clash Royale end-to-end at ~275ms latency, with early results described as incredible.
Two AI agents were pitted against each other in a Doom 1v1 deathmatch—navigating the map, dodging monsters, and fragging in real time—with Laya defeating Jev 5–1 in a first-to-5-kills showdown.
A tool lets an AI agent see Ocarina of Time via a live ASCII-art map, autonomously set goals, remember key locations and actors, and accept hints from Twitch chat messages it judges helpful.

An open-source AI stock trader turned $100K into nearly $210K in a 2022 backtest, roughly doubling while beating the S&P 500’s ~60% gain using William O’Neil momentum rules with same-morning information only.
A computer-use agent demo that navigates automated phone systems (IVR menus), hardened to handle many real-world edge cases.
A Jev-built system that automatically tags and categorizes notes in Obsidian.

A hackathon-built drone simulator where Jev autonomously switches flight modes (hover, takeoff, obstacle-avoid, kill), decides missile firing, and controls four rotors at 2-bit resolution—burning ~$1 per tens of minutes via its high-frequency decision loop with noticeable latency.
4-minute demo: an AI agent farms online Catan beginners with superior turn-by-turn strategy.

An LLM plays Asteroids blind: every game moment is compiled into a number-free plain-English paragraph, then answered through six typed decisions—danger level, turn direction, thrust, shoot, jump, and survive-or-attack.

An AI agent serves as the decision-making brain for a Unitree G1 humanoid, autonomously planning and executing a multi-trip crate-carrying task—hauling 4 crates to a storage rack one at a time then returning to base—scored on trip efficiency.

A Jev-powered app simultaneously identifies CNP trading card types and verifies their physical existence—dramatically faster and more glare-resistant than LLM image recognition, accurate enough for in-app games using owned cards.

A Jev + Reddit tool scans the last 48 hours of posts and comments, uses LLM context filtering to surface buyer-intent questions, and queues them for human-written replies with skip/mark-handled dedup.

A side-by-side email-building benchmark shows Jev generating a complete email in 2.0s all at once (4.7s slot-by-slot) versus 46.3s for the competing approach — roughly 23x faster across 3-run medians.
A re-optimized project now hits a 56-second runtime benchmark, with JEV credited for the dramatic speedup.

Scam Signal Lens, open-source zero-shot scam-email classification eval tooling with replayable results, hit 100% precision/92% recall on English data but only ~17–23% recall on Spanish phishing, where localized questions and lower thresholds helped marginally.
A plugin that scores how likely a given post is to reset Codex usage quota, using a "jev" model to rank and evaluate each post's reset probability.
A Jev-powered classifier that automatically categorizes comments across Facebook and Instagram posts.
Paste a landing-page URL and this tool parses it to rank submission directories in ~5s for $0.004, filtering out nofollow and low-ROI entries to surface only high-DR, dofollow, high-ROI directories.

Turn-based strategy game demo where the in-house AI "Jev" (fixed after an earlier clip accidentally showed a CPU opponent) makes clever moves, playable instantly by tapping the reply thumbnail — 1-minute matches, no signup needed.
A real-time gameplay demo uses Jev, a lightweight classification model, to make game-state decisions in 16 nanoseconds and react instantly.
An AI agent plays a 50v50 RTS game by periodically collecting vision-based intel from all ~100 units and issuing both army-wide and per-unit orders each cycle.
An AI agent transcribes live AFL Brownlow Medal audio to detect each vote, instantly re-simulates fair odds, and auto-places Betfair bets whenever a new edge emerges.

A concept trading desk where Grok agents compress a $1,513 order to $366 and a typed 70–500ms decision model limited to ENTER/WAIT/REDUCE/REJECT rejects on stale data, blocking any broker request and preserving the $7,318 paper account.
A playable band-conductor mini-game built on the Jev engine, where you lead a virtual orchestra through performance gameplay.
An interactive Magic 8 Ball demo powered by the Jev AI model serves up randomized, text-generated fortunes to user questions.
